newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court annuls in part Commission decision on electricity.
newsitem.headline: Court annuls in part Commission decision on electricity.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance annulled in part on Thursday a European Commission decision because it rejected complaints of Dutch electricity distribution companies against electricity import restrictions.

The Dutch distributors complained to the Commission about a cooperation agreement concluded between electricity generating companies and distributor Samenwerkende Elekriciteits-producktiebedrijven NV (SEP).
The agreement restricted imports and exports of electricity to SEP alone and required the parties to the agreement to stipulate in supply contracts they would not import or export electricity.
The Commission characterised the agreement's ban on exports as illegal in 1992, but let stand the import restrictions.
The court annulled the Commission's decision in so far as it rejected the applicants' complaint with regard to the import restrictions prior to 1989, when the Dutch enacted a new electricity law.
EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Dutch)
"Competition - Implied rejection of a complaint - Statement of reasons - Appeal - Referral of a case back to the Court of First Instance - Appeal - Referral -
Case T-16/91 RV
Rendo NV
Centrall Overijsselse Nutsbedrijven NV
Regionaal Energiebedrijf Salland NV, applicants
v
Commission of the European Communities, defendant
supported by
Samenwerkende Elekriciteits-producktiebedrijven NV, intervener

application for the partial annulment of Commission decision 91/50/EEC of 16 January 1991 relating to a proceeding under article 85 of the EEC Traty (IV/32.732 - Ijsselcentrale (IJC) and Others)(OJ 1991 L 28, p. 32)
THE COURT hereby

1. Annuls Commission decision 91/50/EEC of 16 January 1991 relating to proceeding under article 85 of the EEC Treaty (IV/32.732 - Ijsselcentral (OJC) and Others) in so far as it rejects the applicants' complaint with regard to the import restrictions applicable during the period before the Elektriciteitswet 1989 entered into force.

2. Orders the applicants to bear their own costs and jointly and severally to pay half of the costs incurred by the Commission and the intervener each being ordered to bear the other half of their costs;
3. Orders the Commission to pay the costs incurred after the judgment of the Court of Justice of 19 October 1995, with the exception of the intervener's costs, which shall be borne by the intervener.
